Thought: I need to determine what type of material is incompatible with nitrate/nitrite compounds. Let me think about the chemistry of nitrates and nitrites.

Nitrates (NO3-) and nitrites (NO2-) are oxidizing agents. They can release oxygen, especially when heated or in acidic conditions. This makes them potentially dangerous when mixed with certain materials.

When nitrates/nitrites come into contact with strong reducing agents, they can undergo violent redox reactions. Reducing agents donate electrons, and nitrates/nitrites readily accept these electrons, which can lead to rapid decomposition and potentially explosive reactions.

Strong acids can also be problematic with nitrates/nitrites because they can cause the formation of nitric acid or nitrous acid, which are unstable and can lead to the release of nitrogen oxides.

Strong bases generally don't cause the same level of hazardous reactions with nitrates/nitrites.

Strong oxidizers would not typically be as problematic since nitrates/nitrites are themselves oxidizers, though mixing different oxidizers can sometimes cause issues.

Based on this analysis, the most common type of incompatible material with nitrate/nitrite compounds would be strong reducing agents (option D).
